title: 3D Rendering in Houston, TX | 22 Signals
description: 3D rendering for Houston companies: photoreal equipment and product renders, exploded views, architectural and interior visuals, and 3D models for web.
intro: We produce 3D rendering Houston manufacturers, developers and marketers use in catalogs, bids, websites and ads: photoreal product and equipment renders, cutaways and exploded views, architectural and interior visuals, and lightweight 3D models for the web. Renders are built from your CAD files or drawings, so they are accurate as well as good-looking.

sections.h: Why photos fall short for Houston products
p: Photographing a 20-ton wellhead assembly or a skid-mounted compressor package is expensive, and the result usually looks like what it is: heavy equipment on a concrete yard in the heat. Products that are still in design cannot be photographed at all. And the interesting part of most industrial equipment, how it works inside, never shows up in a photo.

Real estate has the same problem from the other direction. A mixed-use tower in Uptown or a new section of a master-planned community in Cypress has to be sold before it exists. Buyers, tenants and lenders want to see it first. Accurate renders solve both problems, and they can be updated when the design changes instead of reshooting. Done properly, 3D rendering gives Houston sales and leasing teams images they can keep using for years, refreshed each time the product or floor plan changes. A photo shoot cannot do that.

p: Engineering buyers in Houston notice when a render is wrong. A flange with the wrong bolt count or a valve with an impossible handle position undermines trust in the whole catalog. We work from your native CAD files wherever possible, check dimensions and part counts with your engineers, and only then work on materials, lighting and composition.

For confidential designs, we can simplify geometry, hide proprietary internals or render only the outside. Files are kept in access-controlled storage and returned or deleted at the end of the project, as your contract requires.

list: Talk: what the renders are for, where they will appear and what source files exist.
Plan: shot list, angles, materials, review rounds and delivery dates in writing.
Build: modeling or CAD preparation, test renders, then final images at print and web sizes.

sections.h: One set of 3D files, many uses
p: Once a product or building exists in 3D, it can do far more than one image. The same model can produce a turntable animation for LinkedIn, an exploded-view video for the sales team, an interactive viewer on your website and still images for print. For Houston firms that exhibit at several trade shows a year, that saves a lot of repeated effort. Because our 3D, video and marketing teams work together, those uses can be planned from the start rather than bolted on later.

We have worked with more than 30 companies across four regions, and rendering often sits inside bigger projects: a product launch, a website rebuild or a paid campaign. That means we think about where an image will be used, at what size and next to what text, before we render it.

3D rendering: Houston projects suit remote delivery well, since every review happens on screen. We work with Houston clients from London, with meeting hours that overlap Central Time. With the six-hour gap, test renders sent at the end of our day are waiting for your engineers when they start theirs, and comments sent back by your afternoon are worked on the next morning London time. Your Signal Lead manages reviews and dates. If we need to see a physical product or a site, we arrange a visit when the project needs it.

sections.h: What affects the cost of renders
p: We quote on scope. For 3D rendering, Houston clients see the cost move with:
list: Whether usable CAD or BIM files exist or models must be built from drawings or photos.
Number of products, angles and variants such as sizes or finishes.
Detail level, especially for cutaways and exploded views.
Environments: plain studio backgrounds versus full scenes.
Extra outputs such as animations, web models or AR files.

p: Our 3D team sits next to our video, web and paid media teams, so your renders can go straight into a product page, an ad campaign or an animated explainer without being handed between vendors. faqs.q: Can you render directly from our CAD files?
faqs.a: Yes. We work with common CAD formats such as STEP, IGES, SolidWorks and Inventor exports, as well as Revit and other BIM files for buildings. We clean and simplify the geometry for rendering while keeping dimensions accurate. If you only have drawings or photos, we can build the model, which adds time.

faqs.q: How do you protect confidential designs?
faqs.a: We sign an NDA before receiving files, store them in access-controlled storage and limit who on our team can open them. We can simplify or hide internal parts in any image meant for public use. At the end of the project, files are returned or deleted according to your instructions.

faqs.q: Do you work with Houston companies in person?
faqs.a: We deliver remotely from London, which suits rendering well because everything is reviewed on screen. If we need to see a physical product, such as unusual finishes or wear, or visit a site for an architectural project, we arrange it when the project needs it. We do not have a Houston office.

faqs.q: How long do product renders take?
faqs.a: With good CAD files, timing for a first set of product renders depends on the number of angles and variants. Architectural and interior visuals take longer because of scene building and materials. We agree review rounds and delivery dates in writing at the start.

faqs.q: Can you render homes and buildings before they are built?
faqs.a: Yes. We create exterior and interior renders from architectural plans or BIM models for homebuilders, developers and brokers. In Houston that often means homes in master-planned communities and commercial projects in areas like Uptown and Midtown. We can match the views to real site photos for context.

faqs.q: Can the same 3D models be used for animation and our website?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is one of the best reasons to render. The same models can be turned into product animations, exploded-view videos, interactive web viewers and augmented reality files. Planning these at the start avoids rebuilding models later and keeps every image and video consistent.
